subject: Physics
subtopic: Oscillations, simple harmonic motion and waves
axis_note: ladder_position is a curriculum coordinate. It is never a learner estimate; teaching depth is intrinsic, while practice percentages only route support.

rungs.aha: An oscillation is organized around a stable equilibrium: when displaced, the system has a tendency that points back toward that equilibrium.
learner_owns: Can identify a repeated back-and-forth motion and distinguish position from direction of motion.
must_contain: A marked equilibrium position and signed displacements on both sides.
Examples where a restoring tendency points toward equilibrium and a counterexample where it does not.

misconception.wrong_idea: Any motion that repeats is automatically simple harmonic motion.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: A ball moves periodically around a circular track. Does repetition alone show a restoring tendency toward one equilibrium position?
misconception.repair: Separate periodicity from the restoring condition; repetition by itself does not identify simple harmonic motion.

rungs.closure: Given three repeating motions, identify which one has a stable equilibrium with a restoring tendency and justify the choice.

controlled_variation.vary: which side of equilibrium the object is displaced to
controlled_variation.hold: the same displacement magnitude and system
controlled_variation.notice: the restoring tendency reverses direction to keep pointing toward equilibrium

rungs.aha: Simple harmonic motion requires acceleration proportional to displacement and opposite in direction, so x, v, and a have fixed phase relationships visible on time plots.
learner_owns: An oscillation has a stable equilibrium and a restoring tendency toward it.
Can read positive and negative values from a Cartesian time graph.
must_contain: Aligned Cartesian plots of x(t), v(t), and a(t) sharing the same time axis.
A marked instant at maximum displacement, equilibrium crossing, and opposite maximum.

misconception.wrong_idea: At maximum displacement in SHM, speed and acceleration are both zero.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: At the instant x=+A, which of v and a are zero, and which points toward equilibrium?
misconception.repair: Use a=-omega^2 x and the turning-point condition: speed is zero at maximum displacement, but acceleration has maximum magnitude toward equilibrium.

rungs.closure: From a displacement-time graph of SHM, mark where speed is greatest and state the sign of acceleration at a positive displacement.

controlled_variation.notice: velocity peaks at equilibrium crossings while acceleration opposes displacement
the plot scales vertically but the timing relationships among x, v, and a do not change

rungs.aha: For an ideal spring-mass oscillator and a small-angle simple pendulum, period is set by system parameters rather than by oscillation amplitude within the model's validity range.
learner_owns: SHM links acceleration to displacement with fixed phase relationships.
Can distinguish a model parameter from a changing state variable.
must_contain: Side-by-side parameter changes: mass versus spring stiffness, and pendulum length versus bob mass.
An explicit small-angle boundary for the pendulum comparison.

misconception.wrong_idea: A heavier pendulum bob takes longer to complete each swing.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: Two pendulums have the same length and small amplitude but different bob masses. Which has the longer ideal period?
misconception.repair: Use the pendulum period relation within its small-angle condition; bob mass is absent from the controlling parameters.

rungs.closure: Predict how period changes when spring mass is quadrupled or pendulum length is quadrupled, and name one variable that does not affect the ideal period in each model.

controlled_variation.hold: pendulum length, gravity, and small angular amplitude
controlled_variation.notice: ideal small-angle pendulum period does not change with bob mass

controlled_variation.vary: pendulum amplitude from small to large
controlled_variation.notice: the amplitude-independence claim belongs only to the small-angle regime and breaks outside it

rungs.aha: In ideal SHM, kinetic and potential energy exchange while total mechanical energy stays constant, and each energy term repeats twice during one displacement cycle.
learner_owns: Ideal SHM has a period set by system parameters within stated validity conditions.
Can interpret squared quantities and conservation of mechanical energy.
must_contain: Energy-versus-time plots for kinetic, potential, and total energy aligned with displacement.
A comparison of one full displacement cycle with the number of kinetic-energy peaks.

misconception.wrong_idea: Potential energy is negative whenever displacement is negative.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: If spring potential energy is proportional to x^2, does changing x from +A/2 to -A/2 change that energy?
misconception.repair: Energy depends on the square of displacement, so opposite displacements can carry the same potential energy.

rungs.closure: Over one full SHM cycle, identify how many times kinetic energy reaches a maximum and explain why total energy does not oscillate.

controlled_variation.hold: amplitude, angular frequency, and total energy
controlled_variation.notice: kinetic and potential energy trade twice while their sum stays fixed

rungs.aha: A wave transports a disturbance while the medium's particles oscillate locally; wave speed is set by medium properties and satisfies v=f lambda, so changing source frequency changes wavelength rather than the medium-set speed.
learner_owns: Energy in an ideal oscillator can move between kinetic and potential forms while total remains fixed.
Can distinguish local motion of matter from the motion of a pattern.
must_contain: A Cartesian snapshot and a time trace at one fixed point, explicitly distinguished.
Two source frequencies in the same medium with different wavelengths but the same propagation speed.

misconception.wrong_idea: Increasing the frequency of a wave source makes the wave travel faster through the same ideal medium.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: A string tension and linear density stay fixed while the source frequency doubles. What happens to wave speed and wavelength?
misconception.repair: Hold the medium parameters fixed: speed stays fixed, so wavelength adjusts inversely with frequency.

rungs.closure: Given two frequencies on the same stretched string, predict the wavelength ratio and distinguish particle oscillation direction from wave-propagation direction.

controlled_variation.hold: the same medium properties and wave type
controlled_variation.notice: wavelength changes while propagation speed remains fixed

controlled_variation.vary: observation from a spatial snapshot to a time trace at one point
controlled_variation.notice: one graph shows shape across position and the other shows local oscillation through time

family.invariant_demand: Identify whether the question concerns local oscillation or wave propagation, select the controlling invariant, translate among equation and Cartesian plot, and check phase or scaling against the physical model.
family.difficult_move: Keeping oscillator state variables separate from system parameters and, for waves, separating particle motion from propagation of the disturbance.
family.independent_check: Use a limiting or phase check: SHM acceleration must oppose displacement, period formulas must respond only to their parameters, and same-medium wave speed must remain consistent with f lambda.

support_ladder.handed_over: The phenomenon is classified as oscillator or wave and the relevant controlling relation is named; the learner interprets the graph/equation and checks it.
The relevant variables are identified and a matching plot or equation is provided.
Only the physical description, measured values, and requested quantity are given.

transfer.changed_demand: A pendulum is released from a large angle: decide whether the small-angle SHM period model is still justified.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: whether the small-angle approximation remains valid for the stated amplitude

transfer.changed_demand: Only a displacement-time graph is supplied; infer the qualitative velocity and acceleration graphs without formulas.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: the phase shifts linking displacement to velocity and acceleration

transfer.changed_demand: A source frequency changes while string tension is also changed; determine the new wavelength after both effects.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: that the medium change alters wave speed before v=f lambda is used

transfer.changed_demand: Energy data are given for an oscillating electric analogue rather than a mass-spring system; identify the twice-per-cycle exchange pattern.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: which two stored-energy quantities play the roles of the SHM energy pair
